    AI Overview
    A rib contusion (bruised rib) is a painful injury caused by a direct blow or fall that damages the muscles, cartilage, or bone periosteum, causing tenderness and swelling. Pain is usually intense when breathing deeply, coughing, or moving. Treatment focuses on pain management, breathing exercises, and rest, typically healing in 3–6 weeks. 
    Key Symptoms and Diagnosis 
    • Pain: Sharp pain with breathing, laughing, sneezing, or twisting.
    • Tenderness: Swelling and pain directly over the affected area, with or without visible bruising.
    • Breathing Difficulty:
      Difficulty taking deep breaths, causing a sensation of chest tightness.
    • Diagnosis: Doctors often use physical exams and patient history to diagnose; X-rays may be used to rule out fractures, though minor fractures often appear the same and are treated identically. 
    Care and Management 
    • Pain Relief: Use over-the-counter pain medications (e.g., ibuprofen) as recommended by a provider, especially to facilitate deep breathing.
    • Ice: Apply an ice pack (wrapped in a cloth) for 15–20 minutes every 1–2 hours for the first 24–48 hours.
    • Breathing Exercises: Perform deep breathing and coughing exercises every 2 hours to prevent pneumonia. Holding a pillow against the ribs while coughing can reduce pain.
    • Rest: Avoid heavy lifting and contact sports. 
    When to Seek Medical Attention 
    • Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing.
    • Increasing pain despite medication.
    • Dizziness, lightheadedness, or feeling faint.
    • Fever. 
    Healing Time
    While pain improves within a few days, full recovery from a rib contusion can take 3 to 6 weeks.
